# Progress

> How far along a task is, or just that it's happening when you don't know yet. That's your spinner, too.

`<slab-progress>` · Data · built on `<progress>`

Docs: https://slab-elements.dev/components/progress/

## Import

```js
import 'slab-elements/progress.js';
```

## Usage

```html
<slab-progress label="Uploading" max="100" value="40"></slab-progress>
```

Screenreaders read how far along it is as a percentage. To say it another way, set `formatValue` to a function of `value`, such as `` (value) => `${value} of 10 files` ``, and they'll read what it returns instead. It isn't called while the progress bar is indeterminate.

## Elements

### `<slab-progress>`

Import `slab-elements/progress.js` to register it.

A progress bar with no visual styles, around a native `<progress>`, so it's a progressbar to the platform with its value and maximum, as one is.

With no `value`, it's indeterminate: the task is under way, but how far along isn't known. That's what a spinner shows, so there's no Spinner.

The label and the `<progress>` are both in the shadow root, so a plain `for` reference names it.

Screenreaders read how far along it is as a percentage. Set `formatValue` to a function of `value` that says it another way, such as "3 of 10 files", which becomes the `<progress>`'s `aria-valuetext`. It isn't called while it's indeterminate.

Style it through its parts and through `:state(indeterminate)`.

#### Attributes

| Name               | Type      | Default | Description                                                                                                      |
| ------------------ | --------- | ------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `label` (required) | `string`  |         | Names it. It's the accessible name, and the visible label where there is one.                                    |
| `hide-label`       | `boolean` | `false` | Hides the label visually and leaves it as the accessible name, for a design that shows the label some other way. |
| `max`              | `number`  |         | 1 when unset, as on a native `<progress>`.                                                                       |
| `value`            | `number`  |         | How much of the task is done, from 0 to `max`. Indeterminate when unset, as on a native `<progress>`.            |

#### Properties

| Name          | Type                                     | Description                                                                                                |
| ------------- | ---------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `formatValue` | `(value: number) => string \| undefined` | What screenreaders read for the value, such as "3 of 10 files" rather than "30%". A percentage when unset. |

#### CSS parts

| Name       | Description      |
| ---------- | ---------------- |
| `label`    | The label        |
| `progress` | The progress bar |

#### CSS states

| Name                    | Description                                                        |
| ----------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `:state(indeterminate)` | While it has no `value`, so how far along the task is isn't known. |
